canonical_topic: Long vs. short exposure, and why 'buy' terminology is misleading for forwards
definition: A trader is 'long' an asset if they benefit when its price rises, and 'short' if they benefit when its price falls; these terms are used instead of 'buy'/'sell' because a future purchase obligation can create either exposure depending on whether the price is fixed.
core_idea: Agreeing today to buy an asset at a fixed future price is a long position (benefits from price increases, since the price is already locked in), while agreeing to buy at an unfixed future price is effectively a short-like exposure (benefits from price declines, since a lower future price means paying less).
key_points: A fixed-price forward purchase = long exposure to the price
An unfixed-price forward purchase = benefits when price falls, so 'buying' isn't automatically 'long'
Traders use long/short specifically to avoid the ambiguity of buy/sell language
trading_implications: Always evaluate whether a forward commitment fixes price before labeling the exposure long or short
The direction of price benefit, not the buy/sell action, defines long/short
caveats: Assuming 'agreeing to buy in the future' always means long exposure — it only does if price is fixed
